info.title: OpenAsy Infrastructure API
info.summary: Hosts, containers and Kubernetes, read without installing anything, with every change kept.
info.description:
Every screen of Infrastructure uses this API, and so can your scripts (ADR 0014). Within `/api/v1` changes are additive only (ADR 0024). Errors use Problem Details (RFC 9457).

Hosts are read over SSH as an unprivileged `openasy` account with 5-minute certificates, clusters through their API with a read-only token (ADR 0031), and BMCs over Redfish by the agent, with GET only and a read-only account (ADR 0055). Each operation names the role it needs (`x-openasy-role`). Sign-in, members and API tokens are under `/api/v1/auth`, provided by [@openasy/auth](https://github.com/openasy/auth#routes).

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: infra-agent: installed once, it reads hosts over SSH. Nothing is installed on the hosts (ADR 0031).

get.description:
The OpenAsy products of this install and their addresses, from `OPENASY_PRODUCTS`, for the product switcher. Empty when it is not set.

Needs the viewer role.

200.description: The products, in the order they are configured.

get.description:
What to put on hosts comes from each agent: GET /api/v1/agents/{id}/setup.

Needs the viewer role.

post.description:
Returns a one-time enrolment token, valid for 7 days. Start infra-agent with it; the agent then has its own secret (ADR 0023).

Needs the admin role.

delete.description:
Only an agent that reads no hosts. Its secret stops working.

Needs the admin role.

post.description:
A new one-time token, for an agent that lost its volume or whose CA changed. Its old secret stops working; its hosts must trust the new CA.

Needs the admin role.

get.summary: What to put on the hosts this agent reads
get.description:
Its CA public key, the sshd drop-in, the sudoers file that matches its script, the commands to prepare a host and the fixed key.

Needs the viewer role.

post.summary: infra-agent: enrol with a one-time token
post.description: Called by infra-agent, not by people. Returns the agent's own secret for every later call.
Called by infra-agent with its secret every few seconds. Each job is leased for 10 minutes. Answers 409 when the agent's version differs from infra's (ADR 0019).

post.summary: infra-agent: send what a job found
post.description: Facts are parsed and masked by the agent; Infrastructure checks their shape and stores what changed. Gzip the body.

get.description:
The hosts come from the hosts file (OPENASY_HOSTS, ADR 0052); no route adds or changes one.

Needs the viewer role.

delete.summary: Remove a host and its history
delete.description:
Only a host added in Infrastructure before the hosts file was the way in; one from the file answers 409 and is removed in the file.

Needs the admin role.

get.description:
The last collection, or with `at` the one in effect at that time.

Needs the viewer role.

get.summary: The host as its BMC sees it
get.description:
Its BMC and whether they match, the parts that are not OK, and its reboots with what the BMC logged around each (ADR 0055). 404 when no BMC is matched with it.

Needs the viewer role.

post.summary: Ask the host for its key again

post.description:
After checking on the host that `ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub` prints this fingerprint.

Needs the admin role.

get.description:
The BMCs come from the bmcs: list of the hosts file (OPENASY_HOSTS, ADR 0052, 0055); no route adds or changes one.

Needs the viewer role.

session.name: __Host-openasy-session
session.description: The browser session after signing in (`openasy-session` on plain http://localhost).

apiToken.description: An API token from Settings → API tokens (`oa_infra_...`): one role, always an expiry (ADR 0003).

Problem.description: An error, as RFC 9457 Problem Details.

unreadable.description: What needs the sudo rules or the container switch to be read.

source.description: file: from the hosts file (OPENASY_HOSTS, ADR 0052); changed there, so PATCH and DELETE answer 409. Fetching its key still works.

fileHostKey.description: The fingerprint hostKey gives in the hosts file: a host that presents that key is trusted without an admin, and no other key can be accepted here.

containers.description: Read containers through the host's Docker or Podman. Access to the socket is equivalent to root (ADR 0031).

hostKeys.description: Pinned. Collection stops when the host presents another key.

pendingHostKeys.description: What the host presents now, waiting to be checked and accepted.

status.description: Of the last collection. new and host-key-pending wait for an admin to accept the host key.

health.description: As Redfish says it: OK, Warning or Critical.

unhealthy.description: Its parts that say Warning or Critical, as the BMC last said.

bmc.description: Its management controller: a BMC that says it is this machine (by SMBIOS UUID or serial), or that the hosts file names with server: this host (ADR 0055).

error.description: Why the last send failed; it is tried again every few minutes.

vulnerabilities.description: Its packages, sent to Vulnerabilities as a CycloneDX SBOM when they change and once a day (INFRA_VULNS_URL, ADR 0031). Null when Infrastructure does not send them.

Facts.description: Everything read from the host in one collection. Values that look like secrets are masked; container environment variables are names only.

source.description: The package it was built from: the deb source, the src.rpm or the apk origin.

sourceVersion.description: The deb source's version, when it differs.

envNames.description: Names only: values are never collected.

caCert.description: The cluster CA in PEM; null to use the system's.

token.description: Token of the read-only service account from GET /api/v1/setup. Stored encrypted, never returned.

ClusterFacts.description: Nodes, namespaces, workloads, pods, services, ingresses, volumes, cluster-admin bindings and recent warnings.

MatchState.description: confirmed: the host and the BMC report the same SMBIOS UUID or serial; mismatch: the file's server: reports another; unverified: nothing to compare yet (the host needs the sudo rules for its UUID and serial); found: matched by them, with no server: in the file.

detail.description: What differs, for a mismatch, and which host the BMC matches instead.

health.description: As Redfish says it: OK, Warning or Critical.

parts.description: Parts the BMC says are Warning or Critical.

reboots.description: The host's boots, newest first, each with the BMC's events from 30 minutes before to 5 minutes after.

fingerprint.description: SHA-256, as openssl x509 -fingerprint -sha256 prints it.

sku.description: Dell's service tag, HPE's product number.

health.description: As Redfish says it: OK, Warning or Critical.

unhealthy.description: Power supplies, fans, temperatures, controllers and drives that say Warning or Critical.

services.description: What the BMC offers on the network: HTTPS, IPMI, SSH, SNMP, KVMIP...

accounts.description: Enabled accounts on the BMC; null when this account may not read them.

user.description: The read-only account on the BMC.

passwordFile.description: The file in the agent's key folder that holds its password. The password never reaches Infrastructure (ADR 0055).

server.description: The server it manages, by its name in the hosts file; id when Infrastructure reads it too.

match.description: Whether the host and the BMC say they are one machine; null when the file names no server and no host matches.

fileCertificate.description: The fingerprint certificate gives in the hosts file: a BMC that presents it is trusted without an admin, and no other can be accepted here.

certificates.description: Pinned. The agent sends the password only to a BMC that presents one of them.

pendingCertificate.description: What the BMC presents now, waiting to be checked and accepted.

status.description: Of the last collection. new and certificate-pending wait for an admin to accept the BMC's TLS certificate.

BmcFacts.description: What the BMC says over Redfish in one collection: systems, chassis with power supplies, fans and temperatures, managers with their network services, firmware, storage, accounts (never a password) and the newest event log entries.

caFingerprint.description: Of the SSH certificate authority the agent made; hosts read by it trust this CA.

enrollToken.description: One-time; start infra-agent with INFRA_ENROLL_TOKEN set to it. Shown once.

AgentReport.description: What infra-agent says about itself on every call: its version (it must equal infra's, ADR 0019), its public keys, and the host setup that matches its script.

Result.description: For a host (hostId): facts (a collection), hostKeys (the keys it presents), or error. For a BMC (bmcId): facts, certificate (the one it presents), or error.

id.description: The product, as OpenAsy names it.

url.description: The address people open it at.

hostsFile.description: null when OPENASY_HOSTS is not set.

changeDays.description: Changes on each of the last 14 days (UTC), by kind, oldest first.

appliedAt.description: When it was last read and applied; null if it never was.

entries.description: Servers in hosts:; its bmcs: are listed under /api/v1/bmcs.

error.description: Why the file on disk is not applied.

warnings.description: What to fix that did not stop the file from being applied, such as a host whose agent is not enrolled yet.

HostsFile.description: The hosts file (ADR 0052), shared with Logs. It is read again within a minute of a change; a file that cannot be applied leaves the hosts from its last good version.
